Empirical Research Plan: “Is there insider trading in CDS markets prior to major credit events?”

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy  
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Method: Event-time difference-in-differences (a “stacked” event study).  

•  The “event study” component isolates abnormal movements in CDS spreads in the days surrounding each credit event.  
•  The “difference-in-differences” component uses the same firms in non-event days and all other firms on the same calendar day as counterfactual observations, absorbing firm- and date-level confounders with two-way fixed effects.

Why appropriate?  
– We observe the exact calendar day on which information becomes public (downgrade, default, LBO).  
– Insider trading, if it exists, should manifest only in the short window immediately before that public disclosure.  
– A two-way FE event-study lets us (i) flexibly trace the daily dynamics of CDS spreads, (ii) difference out macro-level shocks, and (iii) test for heterogeneous effects by the number of informed lenders.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control  
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
D_it = 1 for firm-day observations that lie in a pre-defined pre-event window relative to the firm’s next credit event; 0 otherwise.  
We will begin with a benchmark window of −10 to −1 trading days before the announcement date (τ = −10,…,−1). Robustness: −30/−20/−5 day windows.

Exposure (heterogeneity) variable  
Lenders_i = log(1 + number of distinct banks in the firm’s most recent DealScan loan syndicate). We interact D_it with Lenders_i.

Control observations  
1.  Same firm outside of the event window (before −60 or after +60 days).  
2.  Other firms on the same calendar day that are not within their own ±60-day window around any event.

Event date  
t = 0 is the first public disclosure date of the credit event (rating agency press release, bankruptcy filing, or LBO announcement).

(We are NOT using RDD, so no running variable or cutoff required.)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: Conditional on firm and day fixed effects, CDS spreads for treated firms would have moved like spreads of control observations in the absence of insider trading.  
• Plausibility: Rating downgrades are usually hard surprises, and we absorb market-wide factors with day FEs and firm fixed effects.  
• Test: Plot event-time coefficients for leads τ ≤ −60. Pre-trends should be flat and insignificant beyond our “insider” window.

A2. No simultaneous confounding events within the window (e.g., earnings release, M&A rumor) that are known to the public.  
• Plausibility: Major confounders are rare in the 10-day window; we will code and drop any overlapping events we detect.

A3. Stable composition / no sample selection: Firms do not enter or leave the CDS sample for endogenous reasons related to upcoming credit events within the estimation window.  
• Plausibility: GFI/CreditTrade quotes are continuous for reference entities; we will confirm no systematic quote suspensions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigations  
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Gradual Public Information Leakage (non-insider)  
• Mitigation: Control for firm-level equity returns, inclusion on negative outlook/watchlist dummies, news count controls, and industry CDS index returns. If results survive these controls, they are less likely due to public news.

T2. Market Liquidity / Risk Premia Shifts  
• Mitigation: Day fixed effects already soak up global liquidity changes (VIX, macro announcements). We also re-estimate using CDS spread changes in excess of same-rating, same-industry average.

T3. Anticipatory Positioning by Suppliers of Protection (hedging rather than informed trading)  
• Mitigation: Look at trade direction when available (bid/ask), and test whether abnormal activity is concentrated in buyer-initiated trades; also check that equity short-interest or options implied volatility do not show parallel patterns.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline  
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# Load libraries
library(data.table)
library(lubridate)
library(fixest)        # for high-dim FE regressions
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Load data
cds   <- fread("cds_quotes.csv")      # firm_id, date, mid_quote (bps)
events<- fread("credit_events.csv")   # firm_id, event_date, event_type
deals <- fread("dealscan_lenders.csv")# firm_id, num_lenders
equity<- fread("equity_returns.csv")  # firm_id, date, stock_ret
macro <- fread("macro_controls.csv")  # date, vix, ind_cds_idx

# 2. Merge & variable construction
cds[, date := ymd(date)]
events[, event_date := ymd(event_date)]

# Expand to event-time grid
setkey(cds, firm_id, date)
setkey(events, firm_id)

cds <- events[cds, roll = Inf]   # merge last event on or before date
cds[, rel_day := as.numeric(date - event_date)]     # τ

# Treatment windows
cds[, treat_10 := fifelse(rel_day %between% c(-10, -1), 1, 0)]
cds[, treat_20 := fifelse(rel_day %between% c(-20, -1), 1, 0)]
cds[, post_10  := fifelse(rel_day %between% c(0, 10), 1, 0)] # for visual

# Lender variable
cds <- merge(cds, deals, by = "firm_id", all.x = TRUE)
cds[, lenders_ln := log(1 + num_lenders)]

# Controls
cds <- merge(cds, equity, by = c("firm_id", "date"), all.x = TRUE)
cds <- merge(cds, macro, by = "date", all.x = TRUE)

# 3. Outcome variable
cds[, d_log_spread := c(NA, diff(log(mid_quote))), by = firm_id]

# 4. Main specification
spec_main <- feols(d_log_spread ~ treat_10*lenders_ln + stock_ret + vix +
                   ind_cds_idx | firm_id + date, data = cds, cluster = ~firm_id)

summary(spec_main)

# 5. Event-time plot (pre-trend test)
for(le in -60:20){
  cds[, paste0("lead", le) := as.integer(rel_day == le)]
}
lead_lag_vars <- grep("^lead", names(cds), value = TRUE)
fml <- as.formula(
  paste("d_log_spread ~", paste(lead_lag_vars, collapse = "+"),
        "+ stock_ret + vix + ind_cds_idx | firm_id + date"))
spec_event <- feols(fml, data = cds, cluster = ~firm_id)
iplot(spec_event, drop = "lead0", main = "Event-study coefficients")

# 6. Robustness: placebo windows (shift events 90 days earlier)
events_placebo <- copy(events)
events_placebo[, event_date := event_date - 90]
cds_p <- events_placebo[cds, roll = Inf]
cds_p[, rel_day_p := as.numeric(date - event_date)]
cds_p[, treat_placebo := fifelse(rel_day_p %between% c(-10, -1), 1, 0)]
spec_placebo <- feols(d_log_spread ~ treat_placebo*lenders_ln |
                      firm_id + date, data = cds_p, cluster = ~firm_id)
summary(spec_placebo)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results  
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Theory suggests insider protection buyers push spreads up before bad news.  
• Sign of β₁ (treat_10 × lenders_ln) should be positive.  
• Magnitude: For a 1-sd increase in log lenders (≈0.8), we expect an extra 5–10 bps rise in CDS spreads over the −10 to −1 day window, roughly a 3–5% jump relative to average spreads of 150–200 bps for speculative-grade names.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (Event-study/DID)  
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
C1. No pre-trends outside insider window ............ 1  
C2. Common shocks fully absorbed by day FE .......... 1  
C3. No spillovers between firms ..................... 0  (some counterparty hedging possible)  
C4. Treatment timing exogenous to CDS shocks ........ 0  (firms deteriorate gradually; mitigated by controls)  
C5. Accurate treatment dating ....................... 1  

Total = 3 / 5.
